title: Separating Sampling Noise from Device Conflict in Multi-Backend Quantum Measurements: A Neutrosophic Reading of Simulated Shot Data
abstract: When one quantum circuit is run on several backends, differences between shot frequencies may come from finite sampling or from the devices; Dempster’s conflict mixes device disagreement with the circuit’s intrinsic randomness. This paper reads multi-backend shot data as a single-valued neutrosophic set built from per-backend Wilson intervals: truth is the largest lower bound, falsity the largest complement of an upper bound, indeterminacy the mean interval width, and the contradiction is positive exactly when two intervals are disjoint. This is the conservative non-overlap rule; the neutrosophic layer adds a per-outcome representation, not a new test. A pairwise rule, N2, adds a practical tolerance and classifies each pair and outcome as different, equivalent, negligibly different or open. N2 is a classical three-sided test with a TOST equivalence step; it differs from a pairwise any-difference rule only in requiring a difference beyond for conflict. In simulations on four IBM fake backends, the flag fired in at most 0.004 of runs with identical backends, where Dempster’s conflict stayed between 0.902 and 0.937; the chi-square test was more powerful. In a sequential experiment with non-zero true differences below , rules that test for any difference were correct under a practical scoring they were not designed for in 0.066 to 0.499 of runs, and N2 in 0.725 and 0.916. N2 reported a negligible difference in about half of these runs and in at most 0.008 of runs with identical backends, but was often undecided near and used more shots above it. All data are simulated.

title: The State Is Not the History, the Source Is: Identity, Responsibility, and Minimal Revision in Processes
abstract: A question leaves a demand for a process to discharge; even when several readings agree, an answer must still say which run it belongs to. Through four levels of identity—same reading, same source object, same occurrence, same obligation—we construct a positive chain that the source walks by itself: the original occurrence hands over a complete source program, the program is actually executed and can be read back independently, the execution gives birth to its own responsibility row and pays it step by step, and after settlement the actual action asks the next question. The first link separates readings from sources. Any rooted tree and any constructor function generate a whole-tree program: the execution trace has exactly the budget generated by the tree’s syntax, and a syntax-only parser recovers the whole tree from the program; even when the constructor is constantly zero and every tree executes to the same value, the program still keeps the whole tree injectively. On top of this, the relations generated by derivations and module laws are exactly the evaluation kernel; two source words are the same in history iff at every tick their (old value, effect) difference is explained by that tick’s relations; and the evolution equation covers every element of the completion carrier. When implementations change, the common occurrence generates the unique comparison. The second link lets responsibility be born from the source. A complete environment and expression registered at the original occurrence generate a new mathematical responsibility row without any prior bearer: its budget is the number of remaining primitive computations, every actual execution step is a strict payment, local settlement is reached where the budget runs out, and the completed value equals the evaluation of the original expression; the paid trace is at once a relation receipt, and the whole old ledger is kept as a same-source remainder. For general responsibilities, given a master law covering every same-debt current, genuine payments likewise generate finite settlement histories and terminal receipts. The third link lets an answer ask the next question. After settlement, the actual action puts the paid relation back into the current actual environment: the value of the new request is exactly the effect of the original word under this update, its budget is strictly positive, and its first step is the birth of a new responsibility; the existing inquiry runtime runs through these recursive frames tick by tick, with no external table of future requests. When the old theory can neither express nor lawfully realize a demand, the rooted failure generates a minimal extension: on the ledger, incidence and claim coordinates, every admissible extension receives it through a unique faithful map; every typed revision sends this direction into the new root’s first write, and in a fixed two-tick instance the second tick is answered directly by the same new root. The next question does not set out empty-handed. The same source program folds the complete time of this visit while it executes the effect, and keeps both histories together with an inverse criterion for the action difference; the read-outs of all actors jointly recover the all-word model; the paid query of an arbitrary source program generates a new obligation admission at the same root and visit, and physical and low-level inventories of two types cross the admission and are read back item by item; the default run itself executes this source-generated request, together with its old and next subtrees, paying node by node. A question therefore does not merely wait for an answer: its execution, its settlement and its failure all ask the next question. The theorems and constructions are formalized in Lean 4; complete written proofs are given in the text and the Supplement, and the scope of the formalization is given in Appendix D.

title: Resource–Utility Trade-offs of Higher Reasoning Settings in Large Language Models: Reproducibility Package
abstract: Reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript “Resource–Utility Trade-offs of Higher Reasoning Settings in Large Language Models: Multi-Provider Evidence and Prospective Replication.” The package contains frozen task specifications, deterministic references, scoring and analysis code, seeds, saved scored fields and aggregate results, figure and table source data, and provenance manifests used to reproduce the reported analyses. Credentials and secret values are excluded. Raw provider-response bodies and derived response text are excluded where release rights are uncertain. The package corresponds to the frozen computational experiments described in the manuscript and introduces no additional scientific samples or modifications to the frozen results.

title: How assigned AI use before class shapes active student engagement in class
abstract: AI learning tools are rapidly entering classrooms, but evidence about whether they help students learn is mixed and rests mostly on test scores. Comparatively less research addresses whether the use of AI changes students' live learning behaviors in class. Here, we report the results of a preregistered field experiment with 759 MBA students enrolled in ten sections of a course, in which each student was randomly assigned two of ten class sessions to prepare for with a purpose-built voice-based AI discussion partner. After two uses of the AI discussion partner, students made about 31% more voluntary contributions in each later class session. Students who used the AI discussion partner more also reported greater comfort speaking up and greater perceived learning, but not greater focus or motivation. These findings suggest that repeated practice with a voice-based AI partner can meaningfully increase students' engagement in class discussion, enhancing a critical intermediate learning outcome.

title: QuSema: Detecting Silent Bugs in Quantum Libraries via Quantum-knowledge-enhanced Agents
abstract: Quantum libraries are now critical infrastructure for quantum algorithm development, yet their correctness remains difficult to test. Existing testing techniques mainly rely on failure-based or comparison-based oracles, exposing bugs only when executions fail, violate runtime checks, or disagree with another implementation. Their applicability is limited when suitable execution-based oracles are unavailable, leaving some silent bugs undetected. Such missed bugs can produce incorrect results that propagate into experimental conclusions, simulation studies, and algorithmic designs. Here we present QuSema, an autonomous testing agent for finding silent bugs in quantum libraries. QuSema uses constraints from quantum semantics and documentation as a source-level semantic oracle to assess whether implementation logic can produce invalid outputs from valid inputs. It operates through an agentic loop that repeatedly inspects library API documentation and source code, reasons about the intended behavior of quantum operations, identifies potential semantic deviations, and validates them by generating executable tests through library APIs. Guided by quantum-domain reasoning, QuSema turns high-level behavioral mismatches into concrete, user-triggerable bug reports, enabling it to uncover non-crash defects. We implement QuSema for Qiskit and PennyLane. On a benchmark of 20 historical silent bugs, QuSema achieves higher mean bug relocation counts than Claude Code and Codex, with the DeepSeek configuration costing less than Claude Code. QuSema also discovers 40 previously unknown bugs confirmed by the developers, including 30 silent bugs.

title: Perceptually Aligned Evaluation of Style Transfer
abstract: Style transfer lacks a reliable evaluation standard: ground truth is inherently ill-defined, and existing automatic metrics often fail to reflect human preference. This paper introduces ASTRA (Assessment of Style TRansfer Algorithms), an approach for automatic evaluation of style transfer algorithms; it contains two components, ASTRA-Data and ASTRA-Score. ASTRA-Data consists of a benchmark image set of content and style references, a collection of style transfer results generated on the benchmark set, and user study data capturing human judgements through a two-stage pairwise comparison protocol. From these annotations, we derive ranking-based ground truth for content preservation, style fidelity, and overall preference. Based on ASTRA-Data, we construct ASTRA-Score, a learnt evaluator that predicts preference-aligned scores from content-style-stylization image triplets, enabling automatic and scalable evaluation of new models applied to the benchmark set. Experimental results demonstrate that ASTRA-Score achieves substantially higher correlation with human rankings compared to prior metrics. Overall, ASTRA establishes a robust mechanism for standardised evaluation of style transfer methods.

title: The Future Was Then: The Recurrent History of AI Authorship

title: AI SI — Lightweight Modular Reasoning System with Verified Decisions
abstract: AI‑SI is a lightweight, local reasoning system inspired by TIMDR, built from multiple cooperating modules rather than a single large language model. The system operates fully offline, uses its own learned weights, and verifies every answer through independent validation. AI‑SI does not guess: each response is classified into one of three decision states (confirmed, rejected, or needs confirmation), and uncertain answers are never presented as facts. The system integrates several specialized components: Decision control and verification: three decision states, a safety gate, and a cross‑checked numerical route. Decision loop: when information is missing, AI‑SI asks for clarification and re‑evaluates the answer. Calculator and validator: exact arithmetic and independent verification of results. Source reading module: extraction of values from mixed‑pattern text, with a controller ensuring correctness (96/96 on frozen tests). Word‑problem solver: a combined architecture including a role‑based classifier, a bidirectional context reader, a WordNet verb bridge, and a question‑form bridge. On 1730 real problems from SVAMP and ASDiv, AI‑SI reaches 944/1730 (55%), with 0 incorrect confirmations. Programming module: selection of code examples and execution of tests. Material memory: storage and retrieval of relevant text fragments and sources. Session bridge and strategy selector: a shared session log and a small neural network choosing the response strategy. Polish language interface: SJP.PL dictionary (4.69M lemma–form pairs), a Polish intent mapper, and the Opus‑MT PL→EN translator with number and negation control. Polish question understanding reaches 64/72, and Polish word problems 51/150. nanoGPT language model: a small English model used in a narrow scope. Learning coordinator: safe self‑learning with a growth automaton, preview tool, and weight replacement only after verified improvement. New data modules (7 October 2026): AI‑SI now includes full support for structured and unstructured documents: Tables and spreadsheets (CSV/XLSX): extraction, alignment, and validated reading of numerical and textual cells. Documents (TXT/MD/DOCX/PDF): question answering with citation of the exact source fragment. Dates and deadlines: recognition, comparison, and interpretation of temporal expressions. Unified data router: automatic selection of the correct module based on input type. All data modules pass their frozen tests (12/12, 11/12, 9/11, 4/4, 3/3) with 0 incorrect confirmations. The entire system occupies ~380 MB, of which ~95% is the translator and dictionary. All learned SI modules together use ~14 MB of weights, including ~5.7 MB for word‑problem solving and ~1.3 MB for Polish intent mapping. Qwen3‑4B (2.5 GB) is present only as an offline teacher for self‑learning and is not used during inference. AI‑SI is designed as a modular, verifiable reasoning engine: small networks, explicit safety mechanisms, independent validation, and controlled self‑learning. It demonstrates that a compact system can achieve practical reasoning performance—especially on word problems and structured data—without relying on large language models.

title: Rethinking the Tradeoff Between Temporal Encoding and Nonlinear Computation in Spiking Language Models
abstract: Spiking language models face a tradeoff between representing continuous semantic features over short temporal windows and retaining costly nonlinear attention operations. We introduce Spora, which jointly designs spike encodings and attention operators. Binary temporal weights let $T$ spikes represent compositional values with up to $T$ bits of capacity, compared with $O(\log_2 T)$ bits for spike-count readout. Unipolar Binary Spiking (UBS) uses thresholds and spike-triggered residual decay to produce non-negative integer codes; Bipolar Binary Spiking (BBS) separates sign and magnitude and learns a scale for signed activations. These representations support accumulation-and-shift dot products and integer-exponent mappings in attention. With four time steps, Spora achieves 76.6 average GLUE score and 44.1 CoLA MCC, improving over SpikeLM by 1.2 and 6.2 points, respectively. Extending BBS to six steps raises these scores to 78.2 and 47.4. Conditional-decay analysis, matched-budget activation-quantization comparisons, event-workload statistics, and fixed-point evaluation further characterize the connection between encoding fidelity and computational cost.

title: FoldBack: Self-Correcting Masked Generative Policy for Long-Horizon Garment Folding
abstract: We present FoldBack, a self-correcting masked generative policy for long-horizon garment folding. Existing long-trajectory policies may continue after a missed or slipped grasp even when the garment has not reached the intended configuration. We structure FoldBack's recovery mechanisms around three inference-time decisions: when to refine and verify, how to roll back, and where and how to retry. FoldBack aligns refinement and grasp verification with pick-and-place events, returns the robot to a retryable pre-grasp configuration while preserving successful grasps, and selectively regenerates the failed segment and selected future actions while avoiding previous failed grasp locations. To our knowledge, FoldBack is the first editable full-trajectory policy to unify these decisions, enabling failed interactions to be detected, undone, and repaired before execution continues, without recovery demonstrations or base-policy retraining. Across 33 real garments from six categories, FoldBack achieves 75.2% final folding success and 0.837 final-mask IoU, versus 45.7% and 0.689 for the strongest prior baseline.

title: Beyond Reward Suppression: Near-Optimal Offline Attacks on Warm-Start Bandits with Bounded Rewards
abstract: Adversarial attacks on bandits aim to mislead a learner toward a target arm while keeping the attack cost small. Existing attacks typically achieve this by suppressing non-target arms. In practice, however, manipulation such as fake reviews often directly promotes the target item. We study this gap through bounded offline attacks on warm-start bandits, where an attacker can inject only valid action-reward pairs into the warm-start history before deployment. We show that target promotion is not merely a heuristic: when the target arm lies near the lower reward boundary, any order-optimal-cost attack against UCB that makes it selected in nearly all online rounds must allocate a nonvanishing fraction of its cost to the target arm. We then design an attack that achieves the optimal sublinear cost and characterize its allocation between target promotion and non-target suppression. We further extend the attack to Thompson Sampling, $ε$-greedy, and a broader class of bandit algorithms. Experiments on real-world and synthetic data validate the effectiveness of our attacks.

evidence.title: Beyond Reward Suppression: Near-Optimal Offline Attacks on Warm-Start Bandits with Bounded Rewards
evidence.abstract: Adversarial attacks on bandits aim to mislead a learner toward a target arm while keeping the attack cost small. Existing attacks typically achieve this by suppressing non-target arms. In practice, however, manipulation such as fake reviews often directly promotes the target item. We study this gap through bounded offline attacks on warm-start bandits, where an attacker can inject only valid action-reward pairs into the warm-start history before deployment. We show that target promotion is not merely a heuristic: when the target arm lies near the lower reward boundary, any order-optimal-cost attack against UCB that makes it selected in nearly all online rounds must allocate a nonvanishing fraction of its cost to the target arm. We then design an attack that achieves the optimal sublinear cost and characterize its allocation between target promotion and non-target suppression. We further extend the attack to Thompson Sampling, $ε$-greedy, and a broader class of bandit algorithms. Experiments on real-world and synthetic data validate the effectiveness of our attacks.

title: Constrained Diffusion for Data-Scarce Orbital Monte Carlo in Constellation Tasking
abstract: Constellation Monte Carlo results depend on the orbital population used to evaluate a tasking policy. With scarce reference trajectories, replay limits geometric diversity, while independent orbital-element jitter can violate physical constraints. We study constrained diffusion for orbital-population augmentation. A force-conditioned diffusion model learns a 13-dimensional orbital prior, recovering semimajor axis from perigee altitude and eccentricity; Basilisk propagates each sample under one of five force-model tiers. Using 800 reference trajectories, we compare diffusion with jittered bootstrap, per-tier Gaussian mixtures, and a conditional variational autoencoder, and evaluate distributional fidelity, support shift, classical astrodynamics diagnostics, and 4,000 paired GoDSAT-compatible campaigns. The largest diffusion model achieves held-out trajectory MMD of 0.0171 +/- 0.0239, similar to bootstrap (0.0170) and the mixture (0.0198), but samples farther from training priors (median nearest-training distance 2.7 versus 0.10 standardized units). All generators fail to match the shifted-blind population (classifier AUC 0.991-0.998). Endpoint-conditioned samples satisfy Lambert boundaries but have greater interior error than the matched Lambert reference (29.2 versus 5.7 km mean RMSE). Residual diffusion improves selected sparse forecasts and catalog-mode recall but does not outperform classical estimators on custody ranking. In a fixed 16-satellite configuration, diffusion yields similar mean custody to replay and bootstrap, while the force-tier mixture shifts custody by about 5.5 percentage points. Constrained diffusion supports local, in-support augmentation but cannot replace orbital dynamics or serve as an operational posterior. Orbital-population construction is a consequential source of uncertainty in constellation analysis.

title: Selection Provenance in AI-Assisted Decision Making
abstract: This paper introduces Selection Provenance, a methodological framework for analyzing how AI systems choose, structure, and justify the evidence used in decision‑making. Modern AI models do not simply generate outputs; they implicitly perform evidence selection, filtering and prioritizing information before producing a determination. This hidden selection layer creates a reasoning vulnerability: when the provenance of selected evidence is opaque, the resulting determination cannot be reliably audited, reproduced, or governed.The paper proposes a falsifiable postulate: that systematic distortions in AI‑assisted decisions arise not only from model bias, but from selection asymmetry—the measurable divergence between the evidence available to a system and the evidence presented in the determination. To test this, the paper defines a structured experimental protocol, including contradiction coverage, bias‑interaction analysis, and determination‑pathway tracing. These constructs allow researchers to observe how evidence is represented, omitted, or amplified during reasoning.By treating evidence selection as a first‑class object of study, Selection Provenance connects AI governance with core topics in Knowledge Representation and Reasoning: how systems encode information, how they choose among competing representations, and how those choices shape inference. The framework provides a reproducible method for evaluating reasoning behavior in enterprise and institutional contexts, enabling transparent auditability and more reliable AI‑supported determinations.

title: 构造性收敛的可提取模量：对数级选择器族与注意力核混合时间
abstract: 摘要（中文）：在经典分析中，「收敛」是一个定性谓词；在构造性分析中，一条收敛陈述若不携带模量就不可使用。本文把这一约束推到产出程序的程度：在构造性分析中，收敛率就是一个可被机器提取的程序。以自建柯西实数（零全局公理、语句面置 Set 层、可提取）为基座，本文给出一条完整实现链：（i）Doeblin 单步收缩与 n 步几何率（tv_doeblin_contraction / tv_doeblin_iter）；（ii）有界 softmax 注意力核实例，minorization 常数 δ* := lo·lo 为已证常数，与选择器收束为单一具名定理 amt_attention_mixing_time；（iii）主定理 mix_k_select——对任意 κ∈(0,1) 与任意精度预算，以 sigT 返回可提取的步数见证 k。当 Real 层缺乏 ln/ceil 时，本文不引入新的超越函数，而以 Nat 枚举＋Archimedean 性质直接构造 k；率代数退化端（κ=1 边界）以 Bishop 形全域单调与 Q 载体严格证书互补处置。R1 见证/证明分离路线（叠加 bernoulli 证书链惰性化）已实施并双实现独立验收达标：验收参数（TV₀=1, budget=1/2, κ=1/2）下提取程序实测打印 k=15、墙钟 173 ms（验收门槛 10 s）；新旧链同参对照由 90 s 超时转为 2.09 s 返回。据此主张升级为「结构可提取＋Q 层可运行＋Real 层可运行（单点验收参数下实测）」，仍不主张全域参数开箱即用。对数量级选择器族（二分／倍增／阶梯＋闭式封顶定理）四路径平行构造收束，把返回步数量级由线性关至对数。具体实例层：Fin2 非退化实例给出无条件混合时间界 cf2_mixing_time。模块层追加：混合窗双侧判定（退化世界一步拍平 TV(1)=0；非退化世界精确幂律＋预算下界）、温度-模量引用发散（温度选择是算法的一部分），以及非混合性对照的形式化三件套（nat 见证形主件＋Q 层定理 A＋上界侧膨胀律）。全部结果满足零全局公理、零 Admitted；四关验证（禁词扫描／全量编译／提取 Obj.magic=0／内核 coqchk）与云端 CI 认证在案。 关键词（中文）：构造性分析；显式模量；混合时间；Doeblin 收缩；注意力核；可提取见证；形式化验证 Abstract: In classical analysis "convergence" is a qualitative predicate; in constructive analysis, a convergence statement without a modulus cannot be used. We push this constraint to the point of producing a program: in constructive analysis, the rate of convergence IS a machine-extractable program. Over a self-built Cauchy-real base (zero global axioms, Set-level statements, extractable), we give a complete implementation chain: (i) single-step Doeblin contraction and the n-step geometric rate (tv_doeblin_contraction / tv_doeblin_iter); (ii) a bounded-softmax attention-kernel instance whose minorization constant delta* := lo*lo is proved, closing into the single named theorem amt_attention_mixing_time; (iii) the main theorem mix_k_select — for every kappa in (0,1) and every precision budget, a sigT-extractable step-count witness k is returned. Where the Real layer lacks ln/ceil, we introduce no new transcendential functions but construct k directly by Nat enumeration plus the Archimedean property; the degenerate end of the rate algebra (kappa = 1) is handled by Bishop-form global monotonicity complemented by a Q-carrier strict-positivity certificate. An R1 witness/proof-separation route (plus Bernoulli certificate-chain lazification) has been implemented and accepted by dual independent runs: at the acceptance parameters (TV0=1, budget=1/2, kappa=1/2) the extracted program actually prints k=15 in 173 ms wall time (threshold 10 s); a same-parameter comparison converts a 90 s timeout into a 2.09 s return. The claim upgrades to "structurally extractable + Q-layer runnable + Real-layer runnable (measured at single-point acceptance parameters)"; box-ready, all-parameter executability is not claimed. A logarithmic-scale selector family (binary search / doubling / ladder plus a closed-form cap theorem) closes four parallel constructions, tightening the returned step count from linear to logarithmic order. At the concrete-instance level, the non-degenerate Fin2 line yields an unconditional mixing-time bound cf2_mixing_time. Module-layer additions: a two-sided mixing-window verdict (one-step collapse TV(1)=0 in the degenerate world; exact power law plus budget lower bound in the non-degenerate world), temperature-modulus reference divergence (temperature choice is part of the algorithm), and a formalized three-piece non-mixing contrast (nat-witness main piece, Q-layer Theorem A, upper-bound inflation law). All results satisfy zero global axioms and zero Admitted, with four-gate verification (banned-token scan / full compilation / extraction Obj.magic=0 / kernel coqchk) and cloud CI certification on record. Keywords: constructive analysis; explicit modulus; mixing time; Doeblin contraction; attention kernel; extractable witness; formal verification

abstract: Code and stored numerical outputs that regenerate every number, figure and table of the paper Causal Information Limits of Learning with a Noisy Persistent State (D. Bragetti), including the ball-arithmetic (Arb) certificates behind its strict-local-optimality statements. This record is the reproducibility artifact, not the paper. Start with README.md; checksums in SHA256SUMS.txt.

title: IA nos negócios pet
abstract: IA nos negócios pet apresenta um percurso de aplicação de inteligência artificial para pet shops, banho e tosa e serviços para animais.O objetivo do livro é ajudar o leitor a melhorar organização e experiência para aumentar retorno com serviços adequados e informação confiável. O conteúdo usa casos didáticos fictícios, exemplos e propostas de trabalho para discutir decisões, organização de informações e revisão humana.Ao longo dos 10 capítulos, você encontrará:A jornada do tutorCadastro e preferênciasAgenda com IAConfirmações e comunicaçãoCatálogo e atendimentoO percurso avança até Projeto: uma rotina de atendimento recorrente. As atividades devem ser adaptadas ao contexto e conferidas pelo leitor; os casos fictícios não representam resultados comprovados. Edição digital em EPUB. Página do livro: https://edu.cog.ia.br/livros/negocios-pet/ . O arquivo integral tem acesso restrito; os metadados e o DOI são públicos.

title: The Selection Layer: How AI Systems Choose Between Abundant Intelligence
abstract: As AI systems gain access to increasingly capable and interchangeable models, tools, providers and information sources, the competitive problem begins to shift from generating intelligence to selecting the pathway most likely to produce a trusted outcome. This paper proposes the Selection Layer within the Elsewhere Systems Framework: the point at which an AI-mediated system evaluates plausible pathways, resolves uncertainty and commits to a preferred route for a defined need. It develops the relationship between selection, trusted resolution, reuse and default formation, and examines how the economic value of AI may migrate from model intelligence towards the systems that determine what to use, when to use it and whether a pathway should be selected again. The paper argues that as intelligence becomes more abundant, selection may become the scarce resource — creating a potential progression from intelligence to selection, selection to trust, trust to reuse, and reuse to default. The Selection Layer is presented as a theoretical and testable proposition within the Elsewhere Systems Framework, not as an established description of how all AI systems currently operate.

title: Can Finite Experiments Certify Actual Infinity? Dimension Witnesses, Tsirelson's Problem, and Holographic Resource Bounds
abstract: Whether physical reality contains an actual infinity is usually discussed philosophically. We ask a narrower, quantitative question: what would it cost a finite experiment to certify it? We combine sharp results from quantum information with physical resource bounds. (1) Certification budget. Resolving a game value to ε requires N ≳ ln(1/4δ) w(1−w)/ε² rounds (Bretagnolle–Huber), so the cost of certifying a Hilbert-space dimension D is governed by the gap ε_G(D) between the optimal value and the best dimension-D value. Take the unspecified constants in the known bounds to be one. Then the best known two-player dimension witness needs at least 10⁸⁶ rounds to certify a dimension beyond the Bekenstein bound of a 1 kg, 1 m laboratory (2.6×10⁴³ qubits). Such a laboratory can perform only 2.4×10⁶⁸ operations in the age of the universe. Beyond the de Sitter entropy (4.8×10¹²² qubits), the witness needs at least 10²⁴⁵ rounds, against the 10¹²⁰ operations of the universe. Spatial parallelisation does not help, because the Margolus–Levitin bound limits the total rate summed over all subsystems that share the energy. For the I₃₃₂₂ inequality the requirement is doubly exponential. (2) Embezzlement asymptotics. The optimal fidelity of van Dam–Hayden embezzlement of one EPR pair is F_n = (H_{n/2} + σ_{n/2})/H_n. Hence 1 − F_n = (ln 2 − σ)/H_n + O(1/(n ln n)) with σ = 0.2992041. This holds for all n. It is confirmed to 10⁻⁶ for dimensions up to 2²⁶, and to 6×10⁻⁸ for odd n = 10⁷ + 1. The infinite-dimensional resource behind these witnesses is approached only logarithmically. (3) The Tsirelson loophole. MIP*=RE implies that commuting-operator correlations can exceed every finite-dimensional value by a finite gap, which finite statistics could in principle detect. However, the set of true bounds ω*(G) ≤ t is Π⁰₁ but not computably enumerable. No consistent theory therefore proves all of them, and this route is limited by provability rather than by statistics. In practice, no separating game with small question and answer sets and a computed gap is known. (4) Thermodynamic infinities. Kaufman's exact formula for the two-dimensional Ising model on a finite torus shows that a 1 cm sample rounds the critical singularity at |K − K_c|/K_c ~ 4×10⁻⁹. The logarithmic amplitude of the specific-heat peak equals that of the bulk singularity. The orbital helium lambda-point experiment, which reached |t| ≈ 10⁻⁹, stays about four orders of magnitude above the finite-size scale of its sample. These results do not show that nature is finite. They show the following: apart from one route whose cost is logical rather than statistical, finiteness bounded by holography cannot be refuted from inside a universe that respects that bound. Code, data and figures: https://github.com/Ruqing1963/certify-infinity

For the I₃₃₂₂ inequality the requirement is doubly exponential. (2) Embezzlement asymptotics. The optimal fidelity of van Dam–Hayden embezzlement of one EPR pair is F_n = (H_{n/2} + σ_{n/2})/H_n. Hence 1 − F_n = (ln 2 − σ)/H_n + O(1/(n ln n)) with σ = 0.2992041. This holds for all n. It is confirmed to 10⁻⁶ for dimensions up to 2²⁶, and to 6×10⁻⁸ for odd n = 10⁷ + 1. The infinite-dimensional resource behind these witnesses is approached only logarithmically. (3) The Tsirelson loophole. MIP*=RE implies that commuting-operator correlations can exceed every finite-dimensional value by a finite gap, which finite statistics could in principle detect. However, the set of true bounds ω*(G) ≤ t is Π⁰₁ but not computably enumerable. No consistent theory therefore proves all of them, and this route is limited by provability rather than by statistics. In practice, no separating game with small question and answer sets and a computed gap is known. (4) Thermodynamic infinities. Kaufman's exact formula for the two-dimensional Ising model on a finite torus shows that a 1 cm sample rounds the critical singularity at |K − K_c|/K_c ~ 4×10⁻⁹. The logarithmic amplitude of the specific-heat peak equals that of the bulk singularity. The orbital helium lambda-point experiment, which reached |t| ≈ 10⁻⁹, stays about four orders of magnitude above the finite-size scale of its sample. These results do not show that nature is finite. They show the following: apart from one route whose cost is logical rather than statistical, finiteness bounded by holography cannot be refuted from inside a universe that respects that bound. title: HCFSL-UAV: Hierarchical Cluster-Head Federated Split Learning for UAV Networks
abstract: Resource constraints, time-varying links, and heterogeneous data distributions make distributed model training difficult in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks. Conventional federated learning can impose substantial computational and communication burdens on resource-constrained UAVs, whereas existing split-learning schemes commonly rely on fixed split points and static participation strategies. To address these limitations, this paper proposes HCFSL-UAV, a hierarchical cluster-head federated split learning framework for UAV networks. The framework adopts a three-layer architecture composed of a central base station, cluster-head UAVs, and member UAVs, and integrates split learning within hierarchical federated aggregation. Member UAVs are dynamically associated with cluster heads according to their own real-time 3-D spatial locations. Within each cluster, participant selection and model splitting are jointly optimized as the set of selected UAVs affects data representativeness and synchronous training latency, while the split point determines the computation, memory, and communication requirements of participating UAVs. A joint optimization problem is formulated to balance data-distribution deviation, training latency, and resource consumption, and an alternating optimization procedure is developed using greedy participant selection and a discrete split-point search. Experiments on FMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 show that HCFSL-UAV achieves faster convergence and higher test accuracy than the considered federated-learning and split-learning baselines, while reducing communication and computation overhead in the reported settings. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of jointly optimizing participant selection and adaptive model partitioning in dynamic and heterogeneous UAV networks.

title: On the Cyclic Assumption of the Cow-Path Search Algorithm
abstract: In the cow-path problem, a cow must find a goal lying at an unknown distance on one of $w$ paths connected only at the origin, and performance is measured by competitive ratio. Kao, Reif and Tate designed an efficient randomized algorithm in which the cow visits the paths in a fixed cyclic order. They proved the algorithm is optimal for $w=2$, and subsequently Kao, Ma, Sipser and Yin proved its optimality for all $w$, with a claim that no algorithm does better than the best cyclic one. This note provides a detailed proof of that claim.

title: Temporal Predictive Multiplicity: Equally Accurate Time Series Models Yield Different Forecast Trajectories
abstract: Models with near-identical predictive performance can yield substantially different predictions, a phenomenon known as predictive multiplicity. Prior work has mostly studied this at the level of individual scalar outputs. In time-series forecasting, however, predictions across horizons jointly define a trajectory, and horizon-wise comparisons can hide important differences in predictive behavior. To address this problem, we introduce temporal predictive multiplicity, a framework that characterizes disagreement over complete forecast trajectories among models with near-identical predictive performance. We show that constraining predictive performance alone can still admit a broad range of different trajectories. We further show that constraining multiplicity at individual horizons partially reduces, but does not eliminate, trajectory-level multiplicity. Experiments with 19 neural forecasting architectures on 11 datasets confirm that near-optimal models can exhibit substantial variability in the forecast trajectories they produce, and trajectory-level disagreement is largely unrelated to horizon-wise disagreement. Our framework, therefore, exposes a gap in existing multiplicity studies: models with indistinguishable predictive performance imply fundamentally different temporal trajectories, with consequential downstream effects.

title: A Double-Dilaton Holographic Model of QCD: Running Coupling and Meson Phenomenology
abstract: We present a holographic model of QCD to study the strong coupling constant α_s from the low-energy region to the high-energy regime. The approach uses a double-dilaton background, which breaks conformal and chiral symmetries, while large-N_c corrections are incorporated to connect the holographic description with perturbative QCD. The model leads to an infrared fixed point and provides a smooth transition to the pQCD running. The resulting background also produces linear Regge trajectories for scalar, vector, and tensor states in reasonable agreement with experimental data.

title: A Comparative Study of Evaluation Metrics for Long-Document Financial Narrative Summarization with Transformers
abstract: There are more than 2,000 listed companies on the UK's London Stock Exchange, divided into 11 sectors who are required to communicate their financial results at least twice in a single financial year. UK annual reports are very lengthy documents with around 80 pages on average. In this study, we aim to benchmark a variety of summarisation methods on a set of different pre-trained transformers with different extraction techniques. In addition, we considered multiple evaluation metrics in order to investigate their differing behaviour and applicability on a dataset from the Financial Narrative Summarisation (FNS 2020) shared task, which is composed of annual reports published by firms listed on the London Stock Exchange and their corresponding summaries. We hypothesise that some evaluation metrics do not reflect true summarisation ability and propose a novel BRUGEscore metric, as the harmonic mean of ROUGE-2 and BERTscore. Finally, we perform a statistical significance test on our results to verify whether they are statistically robust, alongside an adversarial analysis task with three different corruption methods.

title: TMT: Runtime Backdoor Detection for Vision-Language-Action Policies on Unseen Tasks
abstract: Backdoored vision-language-action (VLA) policies can preserve benign task performance while producing malicious actions when a trigger appears. Detecting such activation is difficult because malicious behavior can comprise individually plausible actions, while unfamiliar tasks introduce legitimate changes in observations and behavior. We introduce TMT, a runtime backdoor detector based on Token Manifold and latent Transition modeling. Trained on benign rollouts, its two branches assess input-token structure and prediction errors in adjacent-layer latent dynamics. A suspicious rollout identified by the token manifold branch, once confirmed through latent deviations, guides transition selection for subsequent monitoring. We further explore policy purification through self-distillation: a frozen copy of the backdoored policy provides benign-input actions to supervise a student on paired benign and triggered observations, without requiring a separate clean reference policy. For evaluation, we adapt traditional backdoor detectors and repurpose anomaly and failure detection methods as VLA backdoor detectors. In a post-hoc comparison with ten baselines, TMT achieves state-of-the-art backdoor detection performance on unseen tasks across three VLA backdoor attacks. Our project page is available at https://zzr42.github.io/tmt/.

title: Bilingual Evaluation by Phrase Structure
abstract: This article presents a new metric for evaluating translation between two languages. Bilingual evaluation by phrase structure (BEPhS) uses corresponding sentence structure across two languages in order to calculate a translation score for text candidates. By using an electronic dictionary, the metric searches for correlated terms and words, defining the weight of all parts of the sentence. The tests were carried out using samples of texts translated in English-Portuguese and Portuguese-English pairs. Experiments on these two language pairs show the ability for more accurate scoring compared to other classical translation evaluation methods. The results of the experiments were validated by professional human translators.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for CRM Operational Efficiency in Retail Banking
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming customer relationship management (CRM) in retail banking by improving customer targeting, campaign execution, and decision-making. This paper examines how AI contributes to CRM operational efficiency through the lens of dynamic capabilities theory (DCT). The study draws on selected banking cases and combines a survey of 340 professionals from financial and non-financial institutions with semi-structured interviews with managers from three major Croatian banks. The findings provide descriptive evidence consistent with all three research hypotheses. More than 80% of respondents from AI-adopting organizations reported improved targeting effectiveness and faster campaign execution, while more than three-quarters reported improvements in AI-supported decision-making. The qualitative findings support these results but also indicate that the benefits depend on data quality, digital infrastructure, CRM integration, employee capabilities, and organizational readiness. The findings correspond most strongly to DCT’s sensing and seizing capabilities, while evidence of broader organizational transformation is less pronounced. For bank managers, the results indicate that investments in AI should be accompanied by strong data governance, integrated systems, employee capabilities, and organizational processes that translate AI-generated insights into action. The paper contributes to the literature by demonstrating that CRM value is created not through AI adoption alone, but through the organizational capabilities required to translate AI-generated insights into operational outcomes.

title: Controlled attribution of an angle-encoded quantum head on NoduleMNIST3D: per-seed predictions, configurations and result tables
abstract: This dataset supports the manuscript "Controlled attribution of an angle-encoded quantum head on NoduleMNIST3D, with pre-specified verdicts and a replicability audit" (under review). It holds the records needed to recompute every AUC and every AUC comparison in the paper on NoduleMNIST3D lung-nodule malignancy classification with frozen ConvNeXt-Tiny features. A 6-qubit angle-encoded quantum head was compared, on one locked test set of 310 nodules and over 15 seeds, with a no-entanglement circuit, a parameter-matched multilayer perceptron, tuned and larger multilayer perceptrons and an amplitude-encoded quantum head. The dataset contains per-case test predictions for every arm and seed (one long CSV table with 164,300 rows and one .npz file per arm and seed) for the headline comparison, the learning curve (10% to 100% of the training data), the qubit ladder (4 to 12 qubits) and the fine-tuned backbone, together with the headline configurations and Supplementary Tables S1-S5 (Excel and CSV). No images or patient data are included. The underlying NoduleMNIST3D data are available from the MedMNIST project under CC BY 4.0.

title: SwiftGram: Dynamic Lexical Forking for Precise and Efficient Grammar-Constrained Decoding
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) must strictly adhere to grammatical constraints for reliable structured generation in agentic workflows, code synthesis, and domain-specific language (DSL) generation. Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD) enforces this by masking out tokens incompatible with the target grammar at each decoding step, and has been adopted as a core module in mainstream inference engines such as vLLM. However, existing GCD methods exhibit precision defects under grammars with overlapping terminal definitions. The misalignment between LLM tokens and grammar terminals induces terminal ambiguity, where a token admits multiple plausible terminal interpretations. Existing methods handle this imprecisely, causing both false acceptance and false rejection, while incurring high computational overhead. We propose SwiftGram, a GCD framework that incorporates dynamic lexical forking for precise token masking. By forking only at detected ambiguity boundaries, SwiftGram preserves all admissible terminal interpretations while suppressing spurious ones. It builds on Generalized LR (GLR) parsing with the Graph-Structured Stack (GSS) for compact multi-branch parsing, together with adjacency pruning and terminal tries to reduce online overhead. Experiments show that SwiftGram achieves near-zero grammar violations and no observed false rejection, whereas strong baselines remain prone to masking errors. SwiftGram improves effective throughput by up to 14.7% over the strongest baseline under rejection sampling, and achieves a 5.9× average speedup in per-step mask construction under mask-before-selection.

title: RelayGuard: Budget-aware burst shaping against traffic analysis in dual-hop privacy relays
abstract: Dual-hop privacy relay systems enhance user privacy by separating client identity from destination visibility through a split-trust architecture. However, despite this protection model, such systems remain vulnerable to traffic analysis attacks that exploit packet timing, burst patterns, and flow-level metadata to infer visited websites or correlate sessions. Existing defenses against traffic analysis are often too costly for low-latency privacy relays because they can introduce substantial bandwidth and latency overhead. In this paper, we present RelayGuard , a lightweight relay-side defense for dual-hop privacy relays based on budget-aware burst shaping at the ingress relay. RelayGuard transforms observed traffic into canonical burst patterns using a greedy scheduling strategy with budget correction, while encouraging a near-anonymity property through k-anonymous burst buckets , where each bucket is shared by at least k website or page classes. The defense operates on four burst-level features—direction, burst size, inter-burst gap, and burst duration—and applies three practical actions: adaptive relay-layer padding, small delay injection, and short-window micro-batching. We formulate the defense objective as a joint optimization of canonicalization fidelity, anonymity preservation, and overhead cost, and solve it using an efficient online heuristic suitable for low-latency ingress-side deployment. We evaluate RelayGuard in a controlled emulated dual-hop relay testbed under defense-aware website fingerprinting and session linkage attacks. Experimental results show that RelayGuard reduces closed-world website fingerprinting accuracy from 84.22% to 22.45% for a classical attacker and from 93.58% to 28.90% for a deep learning-based attacker. It also lowers page-family-level session linkage accuracy to 38.50% and 46.75% for the two attackers, respectively, while maintaining practical shaping overhead. Additional comparisons against recent shaping-inspired baselines show that RelayGuard provides a stronger privacy–overhead trade-off in the evaluated relay setting. These results suggest that budget-aware burst shaping is a promising direction for strengthening traffic analysis resistance in dual-hop privacy relay architectures.

title: NeuralBES: A Differentiable, Control-Aware Emulator for Scalable Building Energy Modeling
abstract: Demand-side flexibility i.e. forecasting, shifting, and curtailing residential energy loads, depends on thermal models trusted across millions of heterogeneous buildings. Existing tools force a hard tradeoff: high-fidelity physics simulators such as EnergyPlus are accurate but sequential and require per-building calibration, while purely data-driven sequence models scale but abandon the physical structure that makes their predictions trustworthy. We introduce NeuralBES (Building Energy Simulation), a differentiable emulator that resolves this tradeoff by parameterizing a resistance--capacitance (RC) based thermal model with a shared neural encoder: static building metadata such as floor area, vintage, and HVAC type is mapped to physically bounded capacitances, conductances, and equipment coefficients, which become the coefficients of a scalar linear recurrence solved via a log-space parallel scan, and a predictor--corrector loop closes the thermostat--temperature nonlinearity while preserving full-horizon gradient flow. Trained on the ResStock dataset across three climate zones, NeuralBES handles heterogeneous building archetypes, vintages, and climate zones within a single trained encoder, while black-box baselines produce statistically plausible but physically inconsistent trajectories. On the annual full-year rollout, NeuralBES is the only data-conditioned model that is simultaneously physics-valid and accurate to within 4 MAPE points of the strongest raw-error baseline, while operating at roughly an order of magnitude fewer parameters than the transformer and recurrent baselines; among physics-valid baselines at parameter parity it more than halves the MAPE of the grey-box RC alternative.

title: Logarithmic Regret via Passive Change Detection in Piecewise-Stationary Self-Tuning Regulation
abstract: We study minimum-variance control of an unknown autoregressive system with exogenous inputs and coefficients that change at unknown times. Under bounded independent disturbances, fixed detection gaps, stability and feasibility conditions, and sufficient time between changes, we prove \(O((C+1)\log((T+1)/δ))\) regret with probability at least \(1-δ\), where \(T\) is the horizon and \(C\) the number of changes. Unlike switching bandits, where unselected arms can change unobserved, admissible plant changes provide information during exploitation: the correct feasible controller leaves only the disturbance in the output, whereas a detectable change raises output energy under the old controller. PIECE-CD explores initially and after alarms, then uses gated recursive least squares for control. Its energy test compares windowed output power with a threshold above the noise floor; the extension to unstable controller mismatches also monitors the reference controller's input proposal. evidence.title: Logarithmic Regret via Passive Change Detection in Piecewise-Stationary Self-Tuning Regulation
evidence.abstract: We study minimum-variance control of an unknown autoregressive system with exogenous inputs and coefficients that change at unknown times. Under bounded independent disturbances, fixed detection gaps, stability and feasibility conditions, and sufficient time between changes, we prove \(O((C+1)\log((T+1)/δ))\) regret with probability at least \(1-δ\), where \(T\) is the horizon and \(C\) the number of changes. Unlike switching bandits, where unselected arms can change unobserved, admissible plant changes provide information during exploitation: the correct feasible controller leaves only the disturbance in the output, whereas a detectable change raises output energy under the old controller. PIECE-CD explores initially and after alarms, then uses gated recursive least squares for control. Its energy test compares windowed output power with a threshold above the noise floor; the extension to unstable controller mismatches also monitors the reference controller's input proposal. We control false alarms across the horizon and prove logarithmic detection delay. Inputs are clipped to prescribed bounds. title: Efficient Patch-Based Anomaly Detection Fused with Diffusion Driven Generative Modeling for Semiconductor Wafer Bin Map Open Set Anomaly Detection
abstract: Spatial defect signatures on wafer bin maps (WBMs) trace yield loss to specific process faults, yet supervised classifiers recognize only the defect types seen during training, and one-class detectors built on a single mechanism tend to capture either local structural deviations or global distributional violations, but rarely both. This work proposes a hybrid one-class framework that couples a patch-based student-teacher detector (EfficientAD) with a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) used for partial-diffusion reconstruction, and fuses their percentile-calibrated scores through a fixed convex combination. Trained on only 700 normal wafers from the WM-38K mixed-type dataset and evaluated on 18,658 held-out wafers, the fused detector reached an AUROC of 0.9985 and reduced misclassifications from 852 (DDPM) and 1,412 (EfficientAD) to 618, with all pairwise differences significant at p < 0.001. Beyond aggregate accuracy, the analysis shows that the gain arises from weakly overlapping errors between the two modules, yet fixed-weight fusion recovers only 40-70% of the correction available to an oracle selector. Under the benchmark's inverted class balance, average precision and F1 saturate, while the Matthews correlation coefficient and negative predictive value expose unreliable normal predictions. Pixel-level maps further show that strong image-level separability does not imply spatial localization, and the diffusion module succeeds as a local density prior rather than through global geometric reasoning. These findings motivate sample-adaptive fusion and imbalance-aware evaluation of hybrid wafer anomaly detectors.

title: ЕМОЦІЙНЕ ЗАБАРВЛЕННЯ ЗАГОЛОВКІВ АНГЛОМОВНИХ ЄВРОПЕЙСЬКИХ МЕДІА ПРО РОСІЙСЬКО-УКРАЇНСЬКУ ВІЙНУ
abstract: This study conducts automated emotional analysis of headlines from English-language European media outlets (DW, France 24, Politico Europe, Euronews, Der Spiegel International, El País English, RFI English, and Balkan Insight) reporting on the Russia-Ukraine war between February 2022 and October 2025. The significance of this research arises from the increasing focus on media discourse analysis and the challenges posed by contemporary information environments, including high information volumes and the fast pace of life, which hinder detailed source examination and diminish readers’ attention. Media narratives consequently influence societal perceptions and may reduce critical engagement with events. Emotionally charged vocabulary is frequently employed to capture attention and elicit empathy, and can also function as a tool for disinformation and emotional manipulation. The methodology involves constructing a text corpus and applying automated emotional analysis using the transformer-based emotion classification model, Emotion English DistilRoBERTa-base. Findings indicate that neutrality is the most prevalent category (46.43%), followed by anger (17.86%) and fear (17.86%). Disgust is less common (10.71%), while sadness is the least frequent among the identified emotions (7.14%). Joy and surprise were not detected in the analysed material. These results enhance understanding of the pragmatic mechanisms underlying media discourse, demonstrate the effectiveness of transformer-based models for natural language processing, and suggest prospects for future research, particularly in large-scale media narrative analysis.

title: FNE-AXIOMESH: Capability-Dependent Memory and Regenerative Representation Growth for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI)
abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) creates a memory problem: acquiring a new capability can make previously discarded distinctions necessary for future reasoning or action. FNE–AXIOMESH investigates this dependency between capability growth, representation sufficiency, and recoverable operational state. PureOne/FNE-AXIOMESH · Datasets at Hugging Face This release presents an RSI research architecture and an exact finite prime-field reference implementation. Its central mechanism, Counterfactual Quotient Weaving (CQW), couples operator-library expansion with behavioral-closure computation, memory revalidation, reconstruction, and compilation into a reduced executable representation. Capability expansion therefore carries an explicit obligation to establish whether inherited information remains sufficient. For surviving observations represented by a matrix M and a required operational quotient represented by C, exact quotient recovery is possible precisely when ker(M) ⊆ ker(C), assuming consistent, trusted observations. When this condition fails, rank([M; C]) − rank(M) characterizes the minimum additional scalar observations required under unrestricted linear measurement access. Compiled representations preserve protected queries across all finite compositions of the declared operators. Fractal Tethers preserve the missing information needed to reconstruct parent representations from descendants. Recursive reconstruction can proceed from leaf states and retained tethers without retaining internal parent seeds, provided the required maps and information survive. Non-averaging Unison examines the behavioral closure created by compositions of complementary branch capabilities. Recorded evidence within the implemented finite setting includes: 106 passing automated tests: 77 scientific tests and 29 agent-interface and release-support tests. 10,000/10,000 correct held-out composition predictions across five seeded runs. A strong pooled conventional algebra learner achieves the same result. 4,500 controlled erasure trials with zero false exact-recovery certificates, including cases where the system correctly abstains. 1,000 exhaustive finite-fiber identifiability checks with zero incorrect certificates, alongside recursive reconstruction demonstrations. The dataset component contains five seeded experiment-summary records. The accompanying research package includes the manuscript and editable source, reference implementation, experiment results, bounded machine-readable agent interfaces, a claims ledger, and an expert-review guide mapping mathematical statements to code, assumptions, and verification procedures. The central RSI hypothesis is that jointly selecting new capabilities and repairable representations improves subsequent discovery productivity under equal total resources. The proposed evaluation compares this coupling with separately optimized capability learning and memory repair, accounting for search, evidence acquisition, compilation, coordination, persistent storage, and deployment costs. Frozen offspring and unseen-task evaluations distinguish retained performance from improved capacity to discover the next useful capability. The contribution under investigation is the architectural coupling of established observability, behavioral-quotient, and coding principles. The current implementation operates within supplied finite operator families. Neural integration, autonomous discovery of those families, an advantage over strong resource-matched baselines, and sustained recursive acceleration remain open research questions. The release supports reproducibility and expert scrutiny; independent peer review is pending. Made by Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki.

title: A Comprehensive Review On Self Supervised Failure Prediction For AI Models Under Unseen Distribution Shifts
abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly deployed in environments where the data encountered after deployment may differ substantially from the data used during model development. A central reliability question is therefore whether a model can identify signals that indicate an increased probability of its own future failure before an incorrect decision is made. This review examines self supervised failure prediction as a theoretical and practical framework for answering that question under unseen distribution shifts. The discussion connects self supervised representation learning, uncertainty estimation, calibration, out of distribution detection, selective prediction, anomaly detection, test time training, test time adaptation and robust decision making. Self supervised objectives are particularly valuable because they can exploit unlabelled observations available during deployment and can provide auxiliary signals about reconstruction quality, transformation consistency, representation stability and temporal coherence. These signals may complement predictive confidence, which can remain misleading when neural networks are exposed to unfamiliar inputs. The review further examines the distinction between aleatoric uncertainty, epistemic uncertainty and distributional uncertainty, and explains why no single score should be treated as a complete failure predictor. A conceptual framework is proposed in which the model observes an incoming sample, evaluates representation and prediction stability, estimates uncertainty, detects evidence of distributional novelty and converts these signals into a calibrated failure risk. Important limitations include false alarms, adaptation induced error, feedback loops, computational cost, changing environments and the absence of reliable failure labels. Future research should therefore focus on jointly learning prediction and failure awareness, evaluating models across realistic unseen shifts, establishing standardized early warning metrics and developing safety oriented mechanisms that can abstain or request human review when failure risk becomes high.

title: FC-FOLD-019 — Arcane Ring-Phase Autonomous Field Envelope: A Compression and Folding Expedition
abstract: FC-FOLD-019 — Arcane Ring-Phase Autonomous Field Envelope FC-FOLD-019 is a frozen experimental expedition within Field Compute, investigating compression and folding as a representation-search problem across spatial, dimensional, temporal, directional, masked, overlapping, and multi-stream structures. The expedition does not define compression solely as reduction in byte count. It investigates how a representation can be progressively folded while retaining sufficient structure to reconstruct, inspect, compare, diagnose, and measure what survives the transformation. FC-FOLD-019 therefore treats folding as an observable computational process rather than a single predetermined encoding operation. Multiple traversals, directional relationships, overlaps, masks, dimensional projections, temporal structures, and competing folding conditions may be examined before a final representation is selected. A central requirement of the expedition is that compression must remain witnessable. Information that is removed, transformed, contradicted, degraded, or retained as residue must not silently disappear from the experimental record. The resulting representation is therefore evaluated together with its transformation history, residual information, telemetry, and reproducibility material. Scope FC-FOLD-019 explores: spatial folding and dimensional reduction; temporal folding and sequence representation; directional and multi-directional traversal; masked and checker-pattern exploration; multi-stream and multi-view representations; structural overlap between typed representations; procedural packing and representation-dependent folding; contradiction and residual preservation; expansion and re-exposure as part of the search process; telemetry and measurable folding conditions; and reproducible archival of the resulting experimental state. Interpretation This release should be understood as an experimental research artifact, not as a claim that a universally optimal compression algorithm has been established. The expedition instead establishes a laboratory and an evidence trail for investigating families of folding operators. Results are consequently interpreted in relation to the representation, traversal, input structure, residual state, reconstruction requirements, and measured computational cost. The release is intentionally frozen so that subsequent experiments can distinguish the original 019 state from later modifications, extensions, optimisations, or alternative interpretations. Release Principle The governing principle of this release is: A fold is not considered complete merely because the representation is smaller. The transformation must remain inspectable, measurable, and recoverable to the degree required by the experiment. Release Contents Artifact Role FC-FOLD-019_COMPLETE.pdf Primary rendered research and documentation artifact. CHANGELOG_019.md Release history and documented changes. CITATION_VERIFICATION_019.md Citation, provenance, and reference verification record. PRELIGHT_CONTACT_SHEET_019.png Visual contact sheet and release witness. fc_fold_019_arcane_ring_phase_autonomous_field_envelope.tar.gz Experimental archive containing the FC-FOLD-019 Arcane Ring-Phase Autonomous Field Envelope. fc_fold_019_arcane_ring_phase_autonomous_field_envelope.tar.gz.sha256 SHA-256 integrity record for the experimental archive. FC-FOLD-019_DOCUMENTATION_COMPLETE.tar.gz Complete documentation and reproducibility bundle for the frozen expedition. Archival Manifest The release contains two distinct archival layers. Experimental Envelope — fc_fold_019_arcane_ring_phase_autonomous_field_envelope.tar.gz preserves the specific computational/experimental envelope associated with FC-FOLD-019. Complete Documentation Bundle — FC-FOLD-019_DOCUMENTATION_COMPLETE.tar.gz preserves the broader documentation and release material required to inspect the frozen expedition as an archival object. The SHA-256 sidecar file provides an explicit cryptographic integrity reference for the experimental envelope. Zenodo additionally records upload-level file checksums for the individual deposited files. Provenance and Reproducibility This release is intended to preserve not only the final rendered result but also the documentary and computational context necessary to determine what constituted FC-FOLD-019 at the time of release. The archive therefore forms part of the evidence chain. The PDF provides the human-readable research record; Markdown material provides machine-readable documentation; the experimental archive preserves the corresponding computational envelope; and the integrity records provide independent means of detecting subsequent file modification. Status Status: Frozen experimental release. FC-FOLD-019 is not presented as a final universal compression method. Future work may extend, refute, optimise, replace, or reinterpret parts of the expedition. Such work should be identified as subsequent work rather than silently modifying the frozen 019 record. Relationship to Field Compute FC-FOLD-019 belongs to the broader Field Compute research programme and applies its evidence-oriented approach to representation transformation. In particular, the expedition treats transformation, residue, reconstruction, provenance, and observability as first-class experimental concerns. The release is therefore both a compression experiment and an example of Field Compute being used to inspect the behaviour and limitations of an experimental computational system. Citation Vening, Edwin Jean-Paul. FC-FOLD-019 — Arcane Ring-Phase Autonomous Field Envelope: A Compression and Folding Expedition. Zenodo, 2026. title: Antibody-guided chromogenic adaptation for pathology-semantic consistent hematoxylin and eosin to immunohistochemistry translation
abstract: Traditional immunohistochemical (IHC) staining provides essential biomarker information for clinical diagnosis but remains limited by high reagent cost, antibody-dependent optimization and labor-intensive workflows. In contrast, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining is routine and inexpensive yet lacks molecular specificity. Recent advances in virtual staining offer the opportunity to computationally infer IHC appearances directly from H&E slides, thereby bridging the morphological-molecular gap while improving workflow efficiency. This study proposes a controllable multi-antibody virtual staining framework, termed antibody-guided staining adaptation (ASA), which synthesizes four major biomarkers (ER, HER2, Ki67 and PR) from directly H&E images by jointly modeling antibody semantics and chromogenic physics. Within ASA, antibody-conditioned response adjustment (ACRA) provides antibody-specific global modulation through sparsity-regularized and orthogonality-preserved feature transformations; spatial chromogenic adaptation (SCA) performs spatially coherent chromogenic adjustment by leveraging optical density (OD) derived cues; and patch-replacement dynamic switching (PRDS) introduces curriculum-based real-pseudo OD patch replacement to stabilize training under H&E-IHC misalignment. Extensive experiments show ASA generally improves structural and chromogenic quality across most biomarkers, with some metric-specific variations, pointing to its future clinical potential. Our code will be available at https://github.com/youzzz1203/ASA.HIGHLIGHTSDevelops ASA, a virtual staining framework using antibody and OD-driven modeling.Introduces ACRA, SCA and PRDS to enhance robustness under section misalignment.Achieves competitive IHC stain quality across multiple biomarkers.Enables efficient digital pathology workflows via virtual staining.Demonstrates potential as a clinical complement pending further validation.

title: MORCA: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cache Reuse in Video Diffusion Acceleration
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve remarkable performance in video synthesis, but their iterative denoising process suffers from high inference latency. To address this, caching has emerged as an effective acceleration strategy by capitalizing on inter-step redundancy during denoising. Existing dynamic caching methods typically estimate the error that cache reuse would introduce at each denoising step (step error) to guide cache decisions, whereas our concern is how much quality loss cache reuse would cause in the final generated video (terminal error). We show that step error does not directly correspond to terminal error and that latent information helps capture their relationship, thereby informing cache decisions. Moreover, existing threshold-based methods cannot provide precise speedup control, making it difficult to meet practical requirements for user-specified acceleration targets. To address these limitations, we introduce MORCA, a cache scheduling framework trained through offline-to-online reinforcement learning to make latent-aware reuse/recompute decisions under user-specified acceleration targets. Extensive experiments on different video generation models across multiple target acceleration ratios demonstrate that MORCA achieves better generation fidelity than state-of-the-art caching methods under comparable computational budgets. Code is available at https://github.com/x10ngyx/MORCA.

title: Marrying Pricing and Advertising with LLMs
abstract: We study a sequential pricing problem in which a seller jointly posts a price and an advertisement generated by a large language model (LLM). The seller aims to maximize revenue under an unknown product demand that depends on both decisions, while observing only whether each offer leads to a purchase. We propose an online actor-critic algorithm that combines low-rank adaptation (LoRA) of a pretrained LLM with a demand model fitted to available data. At each round, the actor generates an advertisement, and the critic estimates purchase probabilities to guide price selection. Then, the resulting feedback is used to update both the actor and the critic, with the critic's revenue estimates providing a baseline for policy gradient updates of the actor. To evaluate our approach, we develop an evaluation framework with three synthetic demand models and a demand simulator built from real-world marketplace data. Finally, we compare our algorithm with benchmarks that do not jointly optimize price selection and advertisement generation, achieving expected revenue gains over the reference policy of 5.69%, 5.18% and 55.96% under the three synthetic demand models and 5.81% under the marketplace simulator.

title: Beyond Group Splits: Specimen-Level Cross-Validation and Visual Attribution for Remaining-Shelf-Life Regression in Climacteric Fruit
abstract: Estimating remaining shelf life (RSL) from images could provide affordable decision support for perishable produce, but evaluation protocols can substantially affect reported performance when repeated images are available from the same biological specimen. We use the Hass Avocado Ripening dataset, comprising 8,834 image-RSL pairs from 426 fruits across three storage regimes, to evaluate a frozen ImageNet-pretrained visual backbone with a lightweight regression head. Our contributions are threefold: we quantify the effect of observation-level versus specimen-disjoint evaluation, compare lightweight and heavier visual backbones under specimen-disjoint cross-validation, and examine their spatial attributions using Grad-CAM. Across ten observation-level random splits, the model achieves a mean RMSE of 2.37 days with a standard deviation of 0.03 days, whereas specimen-disjoint 5-fold cross-validation yields a mean RMSE of 3.12 days with a standard deviation of 0.11 days. The corresponding mean coefficient of determination is 0.553. A matched per-specimen comparison confirms higher error under specimen-disjoint evaluation, with a probability value below 0.001 across 426 specimens, showing that observation-level partitioning gives a substantially more optimistic estimate for this dataset and model configuration. Under specimen-disjoint evaluation, MobileNetV3-Small (0.93 million parameters) achieves accuracy comparable to ResNet-18 while providing substantially higher throughput, and Grad-CAM reveals differences in spatial attribution between the lightweight backbones. These results support specimen-disjoint evaluation and attribution analysis when assessing lightweight vision models for longitudinal shelf-life prediction.

title: Reflected Anchored Langevin Algorithms
abstract: First order Langevin algorithms for constrained sampling in machine learning, such as projected Langevin Monte Carlo which are based on discretizations of reflected Langevin dynamics, require differentiable log densities that limits their applicability. This paper introduces reflected anchored Langevin dynamics (RALD), a reflected diffusion that converges to non-differentiable targets on constrained domains. The method uses a smooth anchored reference potential and multiplies the drift and noise covariance of its reflected Langevin dynamics by the same state dependent scaling factor. Its Euler-Maruyama discretization with projection gives reflected anchored Langevin Monte Carlo (RALMC) algorithm. We prove explicit convergence bounds and iteration complexity for RALMC in the 2-Wasserstein distance to the target distribution. Numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the theoretical predictions and the empirical performance of the method.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Vision: Beyond Feature-Level Interpretability to Model Control and Cross-Layer Computation
abstract: Modern vision and vision-language models achieve strong transfer across tasks, yet the internal representations and computations underlying their behavior remain difficult to characterize. This dissertation investigates whether sparse representations can extend mechanistic interpretability beyond feature description toward two complementary capabilities: controlled intervention on model representations and experimentally validated analysis of computation across network depth. The first part introduces Visual Sparse Steering (VS2), a label-free, instance-specific intervention method for frozen CLIP image representations. A Top-k sparse autoencoder is trained on unlabeled activations, and the active sparse features of each input are used to construct a test-time steering update. VS2 requires no paired steering examples, foundation-model updates, or test-time backpropagation, and improves zero-shot classification by up to 4.12% while adding less than 0.1% inference-time compute. An exact geometric decomposition shows that uniform sparse amplification contains a centroid-deviation component and an SAE reconstruction residual, linking representation fidelity to intervention reliability and motivating fraction of variance unexplained (FVU) as an abstention signal. Selective-steering experiments further expose a reconstruction-task saliency gap: features important for reconstructing an activation need not be those most useful for downstream control. The second part introduces the application of Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs) as sparse, depth-aware surrogates for Vision Transformer MLP computation. CLTs reconstruct target MLP outputs as additive combinations of sparse contributions from preceding source layers. Reconstruction and functional-replacement experiments identify regimes in which the surrogate preserves downstream behavior. Within these regimes, patch-token contributions are concentrated near their target layers, whereas [CLS] representations receive more distributed contributions across depth. Targeted retention and ablation provide behavioral evidence that highly ranked source-layer contributions identify functionally important structure within the learned surrogate. Together, these studies establish sparse representations as both a basis for model control and a framework for cross-layer computational analysis. More broadly, they show that reconstruction fidelity, task relevance, and mechanistic evidence are distinct. Sparse models are therefore most informative when the structure they expose is treated as experimentally testable rather than as a mechanistic explanation by construction.
